Package hadur117.core.melee

Class StepSurf

java.lang.Object
hadur117.core.melee.StepSurf
final class StepSurf extends Object
MMOVE-28: the step surf, the melee mover behind MinimumRiskMovement.STEP_SURF. Where the ring mover ranks 160 points by a risk sum and hands eight to the waves, this one tries STEP px steps in five directions (the anti-gravity direction with a weak pull to the nearest corner, on, back, and either side), drives each through the WAVES waves that reach Hadur soonest, and scores the path by the damage those waves put on it and the crowd it drives into: 
   danger = (WAVE_K x waveDamage / damageInAir + crowd / crowdNow) x (1 + crowd / crowdNow)
where crowd along the path is, summed over the opponents, clamp(their energy / ours, CROWD_MIN, CROWD_MAX) / d^2 plus a collision penalty. The step is chosen again every tick. No wall, corner or centre term: the posture comes out of the candidates and the crowd. The idea is the melee top's (docs/bench/scalarr-melee-decompile.md, section 3); the code is Hadur's own.

    • choose

      static Point2D.Double choose(Point2D.Double me, Point2D.Double prev, Point2D.Double held, double energy, List<StepSurf.Foe> foes, long now, List<MinimumRiskMovement.Wave> waves, BattleField field, UnaryOperator<Point2D.Double> clip)
      As above, holding the direction of held, the step chosen last tick: a fresh step that way is scored again from here and kept unless another step's danger is under HOLD_GAIN of its own. Without the hold the surf reversed three times a bullet flight and never got up to speed (build 4's read); holding the point itself braked the robot at every leg's end, where the head-on guns found it (build 5's read).
